issue_context.title: systemd-backlight saves value 0 when notebook lid is closed on service stop
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd-254.3-1-x86_64

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.4.12-arch1-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

other

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

When the notebook-lid is closed while attached to an external screen and the service `systemd-backlight@backlight:intel_backlight` get's stopped, the value that's saved in `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness` should get saved into `/var/lib/systemd/backlight/pci-0000:00:02.0:backlight:intel_backlight`.

So when starting the service, the correct value can be loaded.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

When the lid is closed, instead the value 0 gets saved into `/var/lib/systemd/backlight/pci-0000:00:02.0:backlight:intel_backlight` which ends up in correcting the value to 5% of `max_brightness` on service start.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

To test the behaviour the following steps have been executed:

* Connect to target machine via SSH
* Increase Display Brightness on notebook to at least 50%.
* Check value with `cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness`
* Close the LID
* Save the value by stopping the service: `systemctl stop systemd-backlight@backlight:intel_backlight`
* Check the saved value with `cat /var/lib/systemd/backlight/pci-0000\:00\:02.0\:backlight\:intel_backlight`
* Open the LID
* Load the saved value by starting the service: `systemctl start systemd-backlight@backlight:intel_backlight`
* Output: `systemd-backlight[17552]: intel_backlight: Saved brightness 0 is too low; increasing to 969.`

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments: This smells like a driver bug. We just save whatever the kernel driver reports to us.

@poettering So more a kernel issue than systemd?
How does the code retrieve the value? Is there something similar as a cli, so I can test it manually?

@VeldoraTheDragon 
> How does the code retrieve the value? Is there something similar as a cli, so I can test it manually?

Basically, systemd-backlight retrieves and determine brightness from the combination of
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/max_brightness
See read_brightness() in src/backlight/backlight.c for more details.
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/12696a7dbabb1271cbfbaa035c8403ffd62f0789/src/backlight/backlight.c#L386-L443

Please try to enable to generate debugging logs.
Creating the following drop-in config by `sudo systemctl edit systemd-backlight@.service` makes the service generate debugging logs.
```
# /etc/systemd/systemd-backlight@.service
[Service]
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
```

@yuwata 

Well I see where the problem lies.
> Basically, systemd-backlight retrieves and determine brightness from the combination of
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness
/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/max_brightness

When I take a look in `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness` while the lid is closed, it sais 0. 

So it doesn't look like a bug in systemd. In my eyes moreover a prioritization problem, where `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness` is first priority (what I can read with my poor C-knowledge).

And after all things fail. (file does not exist or value is below 0) it fallbacks to `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness`, which in my eyes would be the better procedure for notebooks attached to external screens.

If I would be systemd-maintainer, I would give my issue a `wontfix` tag, since systemd is not only for notebooks.
I should try to create myself a bash-script which overrides the basic function of `systemd-backlight@.service`

> And after all things fail. (file does not exist or value is below 0) it fallbacks to `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness`, which in my eyes would be the better procedure for notebooks attached to external screens.

The behavior was changed in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/16302 because for NVIDIA drivers `brightness` doesn't work correctly... Maybe we should make this overrideable.

Introducing an env variable to prioritize brightness rather than actual_brightness may be good for such case, e.g. `$SYSTEMD_BACKLIGHT_USE_BRIGHTNESS` or `$SYSTEMD_BACKLIGHT_IGNORE_ACTUAL_BRIGHTNESS`.

@VeldoraTheDragon Could you provide the values of `brightness` and `actual_brightness` on several situations, e.g. using laptop display, lid is closed with an external display connected, lid is closed without an external display, and so on.

@yuwata 

For general reference: `max_brightness`
```
[root@hostname ~]# cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/max_brightness 
19393
```

### Scenario 1 : Connected to external Monitor, Lid open
**brightness**
```
[root@hostname ~]# cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness 
15553
```
**actual_brightness**
```
[root@hostname ~]# cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness 
15553
```

### Scenario 2 : Connected to external Monitor, lid closed
**brightness**
```
[root@hostname ~]# cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness 
15553
```

**actual_brightness**
```
[root@hostname ~]# cat /sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/actual_brightness 
0
```

Having the notebook not connected to an external monitor while shutting the lid, getting the value via ssh is impossible, since the device is in suspend mode. When deactivating suspend completely, the value of `actual_brightness` matches with the value of `brightness`. So it looks like, the problem is only present, when the device is connected to an external monitor and having the lid shut. Then, the value in `actual_brightness` is 0.

---

> Introducing an env variable to prioritize brightness rather than actual_brightness may be good for such case, e.g. $SYSTEMD_BACKLIGHT_USE_BRIGHTNESS or $SYSTEMD_BACKLIGHT_IGNORE_ACTUAL_BRIGHTNESS.

this could actually be a way to workaround this issue, without having to revert anything of the nvidia changes.
Making reading the value of `actual_brightness` default, but overrideable for others.

---

Another option would be, if the "correction" value could be overrideable. Instead by default 5% of the `max_brightness`, it could be configured to e.g. 50% by using an environment-variable.

> Another option would be, if the "correction" value could be overrideable. Instead by default 5% of the `max_brightness`, it could be configured to e.g. 50% by using an environment-variable.

I noticed we have already introduced to support `ID_BACKLIGHT_CLAMP` udev boolean property. It may be better to make the property also take a percentage.
Fix is waiting in #29443. If you'd like, please test the PR.

review_comments:
maybe just make this return the percentage as `int`, and return 0 if we shall not clamp?

(and maybre rename to shall_clamp_percent()?

I initially thought so, but people may want to set `ID_BACKLIGHT_CLAMP=0%`, to set the minimum brightness 1. To support such, we need to return `true` with `*ret = 0`. So, I'd like to keep the code as is.
